newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI OIL FIRM PTT SAYS TO REVISE NAT GAS DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: THAI OIL FIRM PTT SAYS TO REVISE NAT GAS DEMAND.

text.p: A decision by Thailand to buy natural gas from Indonesia's Natuna field or LNG from Oman will partly hinge on revised demand projections reflecting Thailand economic malaise, a senior official from state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand said on Thursday.
PTT will adjust its natural gas procurement strategies in accordance with the revision as the demand has dropped by 10 percent this year, Anon Sirisaengtaksin, deputy president of PTT Gas said.

"The natural gas from these two sources is a zero sum game. If we buy from one source, we have to forego the other because the country's demand is not that high. With the drop in demand, we might even have to delay the purchase schedule," he said.
"In whatever case, we will choose the one that offers the best price, long-term security and application for both electricity generation and the petrochemical industry," he said.
Thailand's economy is facing a crisis following a prolonged boom which saw heavy overseas borrowing and a misallocation of resources to unproductive sectors.
The country has turned to the IMF for technical and financial support to put the economy back on track.
Although the government said it expects a recovery by 1999, some analysts believe it could take longer.
Thailand will have to decide soon whether to buy LNG from Oman or natural gas from Indonesia's huge Natuna field.
Industry Minister Korn Dabbransi told Reuters earlier that he would make the decision in September.

In August 1996 Thailand signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to buy up to 2.2 million tonnes of LNG per year over 25 years from Oman. Oman will supply one million tonnes of LNG annually starting in 2003, and the volume would increase to two million tonnes in 2005.
But it has yet to sign a purchase contract with Oman.
The country also signed an MOU to buy up to one billion cubic feet per day from Natuna.
